title: Company-wide policies and processes
author: Sofia Ramirez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating processes across access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It provides high-level principles, owner responsibilities, approval matrices, and links to operational checklists and templates.

Audience: All Redwood employees and contractors. Teams should adapt the operational detail to local needs but must follow the approval and security gates defined below.

Owners & escalation
- Primary owner: People Operations (people-ops).
- Secondary owners: Finance & Legal (procurement, vendor management); Security (access control, data protections); Engineering (change management operational runbooks).
- Escalation path: Team lead -> functional owner -> People Ops -> CTO/Head of Security/Head of Finance depending on topic. For security incidents, follow the Incident Response runbook and notify Security immediately.

1) Access & Permissions
Principles:
- Least privilege by default. Roles grant the minimum privileges required.
- Access requests must be documented, approved, and time-limited when appropriate (e.g., contractor access).
- Regular access reviews (quarterly) for privileged roles.

Role-based access model:
- Employee roles (e.g., engineer, product, finance) map to role profiles in the identity provider (IdP). Role profiles define group membership for cloud accounts, SaaS apps, and internal services.

Request workflow (standard access):
1. User submits request via the Access Request template (Confluence link in Templates section).
2. Requesting manager verifies business justification.
3. Functional owner approves (application owner or team lead).
4. IAM admin implements access and records request in the access log.

Approval matrix (examples):
| Resource type | Approver | Additional approval required |
|---------------|----------|-----------------------------|
| SaaS app (read-only) | Manager | None |
| Production infra (read) | Team lead + SRE owner | Security review if new tool |
| Production infra (write/admin) | Service owner + Security | People Ops for contractor requests |

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Emergency temporary creds are available via the break-glass process. Requests must be submitted after the fact and include justification and post-access audit. Security will perform a mandatory review within 48 hours.

Access reviews and offboarding:
- Quarterly automated reports are generated from the IdP and cloud accounts. Managers must certify team membership and permissions.
- Offboarding checklist must be completed within 24 hours of termination/resignation effective date; contractors require immediate deprovisioning at contract end.

2) Change Management
Scope and definitions:
- Routine change: low-risk (configuration tweaks, non-production infra) \u2014 no CAB required but must follow runbook.
- Standard change: pre-authorized, repeatable changes with a documented testing and rollback plan.
- Significant change: new service rollouts, production schema migrations, or anything that could impact availability or compliance; requires CAB and change request (CR) approval.

Change request flow:
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) using the template. Include scope, owner, test plan, rollback plan, and telemetry/alerts to monitor.
2. Triage by Engineering Ops within 2 business days.
3. For Significant changes, schedule for the next CAB. CAB meets weekly; emergency CABs can be convened.
4. After approval, implement in staging, run the rollout plan, and deploy to production during agreed maintenance windows.

CAB (Change Advisory Board):
- Members: Engineering Ops, SRE, Security, Product representative, and Finance when cost/contract impact is present.
- Approval criteria: risk assessment, rollback strategy, monitoring/alerting, and communication plan.

Testing, rollout, and rollback:
- All production changes must include automated smoke-tests and observability checks.
- Canary or phased rollouts are preferred where possible.
- Rollback must be tested in staging and executed automatically if critical SLOs are breached.

3) Data Management
Data classification:
- PUBLIC \u2014 safe for external exposure.
- INTERNAL \u2014 company-internal but not sensitive.
- CONFIDENTIAL \u2014 sensitive business data (contracts, PII limited, revenue data).
- RESTRICTED \u2014 regulated data (HIPAA, PCI, customer-protected data).

Handling rules by classification:
- Encryption: All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest and in transit (KMS/HSM integration required for RESTRICTED).
- Access: Follow a need-to-know model; RESTRICTED requires explicit approval and signing of an NDA if vendor or contractor involved.
- Storage: Avoid storing RESTRICTED data in third-party SaaS without an approved Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and encryption.

Retention & deletion:
- Default retention schedule: logs 90 days, internal docs 3 years, financial records 7 years (subject to legal requirements).
- Data retention exceptions must be approved by Finance & Legal.

Backups & recovery:
- Critical systems have daily backups with monthly restore tests. Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) targets are documented in each service runbook.

Data access reviews and audits:
- Security runs quarterly access reviews for CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED datasets. Audit logs must be retained according to retention policy and be searchable for incident response.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Procurement thresholds and approvals:
| Amount | Approval required | Procurement process |
|--------|-------------------|---------------------|
| <$1,000 | Manager | Standard PO/expense form |
| $1,000\u2013$25,000 | Department head + Finance | Purchase Order (PO) required |
| >$25,000 | Head of Department + Finance Approval + Legal review (if contract) | Formal procurement, RFP suggested for >$100k |

Preferred vendors & contracts:
- Use approved vendor list maintained by Finance. Exceptions require an approved Vendor Exception Form.

Expense policy highlights:
- Business travel should be booked via approved travel portal; economy fares are standard unless pre-approved.
- Receipts required for all expenses; submit within 30 days.
- Per diem and mileage rules are in the Travel section and Expense Templates.

Purchase order & invoice process:
1. Requestor completes PO request with justification and budget code.
2. Finance issues PO and routes to vendor.
3. Vendor invoices are matched to PO; discrepancies require vendor contact and Finance mediation.

5) Vendor Management
Onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Security questionnaire completed and scored.
- Legal contract (DPA/SLA) signed where applicable.
- Finance PO or procurement record created.
- Vendor contact and escalation list recorded.

Third-party risk assessment:
- Vendors handling CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data require a security assessment (self-attestation + SOC2 or equivalent). Security will assign a risk rating and remediation plan.

Contract terms and renewals:
- Standard contract term is 12 months; auto-renewals must be reviewed 60 days prior.
- Finance tracks renewal dates and will coordinate negotiation and legal review.

Vendor offboarding:
- Revoke all accounts and API keys, return or delete data per contract, and confirm data destruction where required.

6) Travel Policy (business travel and expense guidance)
Booking & approvals:
- All travel requests >$1,000 estimated must include manager approval and travel pre-approval form.
- Use the approved travel portal for booking to ensure corporate rates and insurance coverage.

Allowable expenses & reimbursement:
- Covered expenses: airfare (economy unless pre-approved), ground transport, lodging (standard room), meals, reasonable business incidental expenses.
- Non-reimbursable: personal entertainment, expenses for family, or upgrades without approval.

Safety & emergency:
- Employees traveling to higher-risk geographies must register travel with People Ops and Security.
- Emergency contact and incident procedures are in the Travel Safety runbook.

7) Internal Templates & Forms (location and usage)
- Access Request template: /confluence/templates/access-request (use for provisioning requests).
- Change Request template: /confluence/templates/change-request.
- Purchase Request / PO template: /confluence/templates/purchase-request.
- Vendor Onboarding checklist: /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding.
- Travel Request form: /confluence/templates/travel-request.

How to use templates:
1. Copy template to your team space.
2. Fill required fields and attach supporting docs.
3. Route to approvers listed in the relevant section.

If you're unsure which policy applies, contact People Ops for routing. This document is the canonical index for company-wide operational policies; team-level runbooks should link back to these rules and follow the approval gates described above.
